title: Operational clearance update and customer action summary — draft
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a customer-facing communications draft and internal checklist for the delivery team to publish status updates and a short post-incident summary after the inference latency surge affecting select EU regions on 2029-09-10. Primary audience: affected customers, partner integrations, and account teams. Secondary audience: broader tenant base for transparency.

Executive TL;DR (for status page headline) – short: 
We experienced increased inference latency in EU regions between ~2029-09-10 03:15 UTC and 2029-09-10 07:40 UTC; normal service restored at 07:40 UTC. Root cause: an autoscaling coordination bug that caused uneven GPU pool resizing and queued requests; we implemented a coordinated rollback of the autoscaler, patched the coordination logic, and validated recovery. No customer data loss reported.

Draft statuspage posts (short, chronological):
1) 03:22 UTC (investigating): 
Customers in EU regions may see increased latency or delayed responses; our team is investigating. We'll post periodic updates and recommended mitigations shortly.

2) 04:30 UTC (update): 
We identified uneven autoscaler behavior in the eu-west cluster that is causing request queuing. Mitigation steps in progress: partial routing away from impacted pools and temporary autoscaler rollback. We will provide an estimated time to recovery in the next update.

3) 07:40 UTC (resolved): 
All EU inference endpoints are operating within normal latency bounds. We rotated routing to healthy pools and deployed a coordination patch. If you still see elevated latency, please contact support with request IDs. Full customer summary to follow.

Customer-facing post-incident summary (concise):
What happened
- Between 03:15–07:40 UTC on 2029-09-10, a subset of EU inference pools experienced an unexpected series of autoscaler coordination events that led to capacity thrashing and request queueing. Some requests experienced latencies beyond SLA targets and a small fraction timed out.

Who was impacted
- Customers routed to the eu-west and eu-central inference pools during the event window. Impact varied by tenant depending on pinned capacity and routing policy; customers on Dedicated reservations were largely unaffected.

Immediate actions we took
- Rolled back the autoscaler coordination change to stop thrashing.
- Rerouted traffic away from impacted pools and enabled pre-warmed standby capacity for high-tier customers.
- Deployed a patch that prevents rapid scale-down during transient load spikes.
- Opened dedicated support channels for impacted accounts and collected request IDs for replay/verification.

Root cause (non-technical summary)
- A coordination change to the autoscaler introduced a race condition when multiple scale events overlapped on the same pool. The race led to premature scale-downs and jitter in available capacity, which allowed request queues to grow and surface as elevated latency or timeouts.

Technical details (for engineers)
- The autoscaler coordination algorithm used a lockless compare-and-update path that assumed monotonic scale events. Under a burst of concurrent scale decisions, two controllers could both observe 'stale' capacity and issue conflicting resize operations. The result: one controller scaled down while another queued new work, creating a capacity shortfall for ongoing connections and leading to high queue lengths.
- The patch implemented: serialized decision commits through a lightweight coordination leader lease and added a safety window that defers aggressive scale-downs until a short cooldown elapses when queues are non-zero.

Customer actions (recommended, short checklist)
- If you saw elevated latency: capture one or two example request IDs and send to support (support@redwood.ai) or attach to your account case.
- If you operate a multi-region deployment: temporarily enable cross-region failover until we deliver a full verification (instructions link below).
- If you use pinned capacity: validate your reservations and notify your account rep if you need temporary burst credits while we complete the follow-up.

How we validated recovery
- Synthetic workload replay across eu-west/eu-central for 90 minutes with representative sequence length distribution.
- Token-level latency histograms show P95/P99 returned to baseline within 22 minutes of rollback.
- Sanity checks: prompt fidelity tests, embedding consistency checks, and KV-cache integrity scans.

Customer-facing FAQ (short)
Q: Was customer data exposed or lost?
A: No evidence of data loss or exposure. The incident impacted compute capacity and queuing only.

Q: Will I be billed for failed requests/timeouts?
A: We will not charge for requests that returned explicit timeouts during the incident window; billing adjustments will be applied automatically for impacted accounts.

Q: When will a full RCA be published?
A: We expect to publish a detailed postmortem with root cause analysis and long-term mitigations by 2029-09-20.

Follow-up commitments to customers
- Short-term (this week): account-level reconcilation for impacted requests, billing credits applied where appropriate, and a walk-through with impacted customers on request replay if needed.
- Medium-term (2–4 weeks): rollout of a hardened autoscaler coordination release across regions, additional chaos-testing for concurrent scale events, and enhanced observability (leader lease metrics and queue-length alerts per pool).
- Long-term (quarterly): improvements to routing resilience (cross-region warming), tenant-visible remediation playbooks, and developer-facing guidance on optimal routing/priority configs.

Internal checklist for publishing and handoff (operational steps):
- [ ] Prepare and post initial statuspage message (use the text above).
- [ ] Notify account execs and post the customer list to #cs-incident-ops channel.
- [ ] Open support cases for manually-replayed requests and attach evidence bundle.
- [ ] Trigger billing adjustment workflow for timed-out requests in the incident window.
- [ ] Schedule customer-facing webinar for top 10 impacted accounts (if requested).

Suggested account-facing email template (short):
Subject: Incident summary — EU latency event (2029-09-10)
Body: Hello <CustomerName>,
We want to inform you of an infrastructure event that affected some inference requests in EU regions on 2029-09-10. We have restored normal operations and applied fixes to prevent recurrence. We are applying billing adjustments and are available to review impacted requests. Please reply with a sample request ID or open a support case and mention JIRA-INF-7623.

Notes / open questions (internal):
- Confirm exact list of tenants routed to impacted pools during 03:15–07:40 UTC (SRE to produce).
- Validate billing exclusion list against support timestamps (Billing and CS).
- Verify chaos-test coverage for leader-lease recovery path (Applied ML + SRE).

Owner for customer comms and next updates:
- Primary: Ava Martinez (Customer Success)
- Technical lead for follow-up: Rohan Patel (SRE)
summary: Draft status page messages, customer post-incident summary, recommended customer actions, internal checklist and follow-ups for an EU-region latency incident on 2029-09-10.
notes: This doc is a working draft intended for rapid iteration with SRE and Product before we publish the statuspage entry and the customer email. Replace bracketed fields (e.g., <CustomerName>) before sending.
